description: We're excited to combine our skills, share ideas, and build something cool for this NASA hackathon!
summary:
P.U.L.S.A.R. (Physiological Unit for Life-Support & Autonomous Readings) is an AI-powered health monitoring application designed to help astronauts track and manage their physical and mental well-being during space missions.

Our platform combines daily health check-ins, biometric data collected through sensors integrated into astronauts' clothing, and health trends to give astronauts a clearer understanding of their overall health. All devices can connect locally without requiring an external internet connection, allowing continuous monitoring even in environments with limited connectivity.

By combining NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) research with AI, P.U.L.S.A.R. aims to recognize unusual patterns, identify potential health risks, and provide personalized recommendations.

During long-duration space missions, access to medical professionals can be limited, making early detection of health changes essential. Our goal is to help astronauts better understand their health and make informed decisions, even when they are millions of miles from Earth.

Looking ahead, P.U.L.S.A.R. could contribute to safer and more independent space exploration while inspiring similar healthcare solutions for remote communities on Earth, where immediate medical assistance may not always be available.
details:
How It Works

P.U.L.S.A.R. brings together different types of health information to help astronauts monitor their well-being throughout space missions. Through daily check-ins, astronauts can report their sleep quality, mood, stress levels, and overall condition. Sensors integrated into their clothing provide additional measurements, including heart rate, temperature, and movement.

The application organizes this information into an interactive dashboard where astronauts can monitor their vital signs, review health trends, and track changes over time.

P.U.L.S.A.R. supports four operating environments: Spacecraft, Space Station, Planetary Rover, and Planetary/Lunar Surface. Astronauts can manually select their environment and switch between Inside and Outside Modes depending on their activities. Inside Mode focuses on everyday health monitoring in protected environments, while Outside Mode prioritizes real-time biometric readings and potential health risks during extravehicular activities (EVAs). This allows the application to adapt its monitoring approach to different situations throughout a mission.

NASA OSDR and AI Integration

NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) provides scientific data from studies examining how spaceflight affects the human body. P.U.L.S.A.R. accesses this research through the OSDR API, using Python to retrieve, filter, and process relevant data for its health analysis.

Google Gemini AI uses this information alongside the astronaut's daily check-ins and biometric readings to analyze health patterns, identify potential health risks, and generate personalized recommendations. This helps astronauts better understand their health and recognize problems before they become more serious.

Tools and Technologies

  • Python: Research data retrieval, processing, and health analysis.
  • C: Microcontroller programming and sensor data collection.
  • TypeScript and React: Web application development, including the interactive dashboard, daily check-ins, and monitoring features.
  • Google AI Studio: Interface design and development.
  • Google Gemini AI: Health data interpretation and personalized recommendations.
  • NASA OSDR API: Access to scientific research and data from spaceflight studies.

The hardware includes sensors designed to be integrated into astronauts' clothing, including an APDS sensor adapted for heart rate monitoring using photoplethysmography (PPG), a technique that detects changes in blood flow through reflected infrared light. The APDS also supports gesture detection, while the LSM6DSOX tracks movement and the DHT22 measures temperature and humidity.

Creativity and Innovation

P.U.L.S.A.R. combines wearable sensors, AI-powered health analysis, NASA's spaceflight research, and mental health monitoring in a single platform. Its flexible monitoring modes respond to different mission environments, while personalized recommendations and real-time alerts help astronauts stay informed about their condition.

By connecting real-time measurements, personal health information, and scientific research, P.U.L.S.A.R. makes it easier for astronauts to understand their health without navigating complex medical data.

Challenges and Future Impact

Limited medical assistance, communication delays, and the physical and psychological demands of long-duration missions were important considerations in the application's design. Accessibility and ease of use were also priorities, particularly in situations where astronauts need to assess their condition quickly.

As missions extend farther from Earth, P.U.L.S.A.R. could support greater astronaut independence and safer exploration. Its approach could eventually inspire similar monitoring systems for remote communities on Earth.
